title: Under-Sink Water Filter Installation: Copper-to-Plastic Connections and Leak-Prevention

locations.name: Under the sink (explicit)

locations.name: Basement shut-off valve location (explicit)

summary: This Old House demonstrates installing an under-sink water filter by tying into the home’s cold-water supply, fitting copper-to-plastic connections, and mounting the filter beneath the sink. The steps shown include turning off the basement shut-off, separating existing fittings, applying Teflon tape, assembling a copper branch with a T and quarter-inch branch, installing an inline shut-off valve, using ferrule/insert compression fittings, removing the soap dispenser to access the mounting surface, securing the filter with washers and a lock nut, trimming tubing to length, pushing tubing into connectors, and finally testing the line by re-opening the supply and verifying leaks and air purge.

sections.title: Prepare cold-water feed and establish threaded hardware
concepts: under-sink installation
two copper water supply lines (~1/2 inch)
identify cold supply on left in this setup
break apart existing male adapter and nut
Teflon tape on parallel threaded joints
threading and tightening with wrenches
sections.description: The installer identifies the under-sink area, notes the cold supply line, shuts the basement valve, and begins preparing the copper-to-filter supply by breaking apart fittings, applying Teflon tape, and assembling a T with a branch for a quarter-inch line. Fittings are tightened with pliers and two-wrench technique.

sections.title: Attach plastic tubing to copper and install inline shut-off
concepts: inline shut-off valve included with the filter
plumbing fittings: nut, male adapter, and ferrule
insert and tighten to create a secure seal
transition from copper to plastic tubing
sections.description: A plastic-to-copper transition is created with an inline shut-off valve supplied with the filter. The installer threads a coupling and ferrule, uses an insert to reinforce the plastic tubing, and tightens the assembly to secure the connection.

sections.title: Remove soap dispenser and prepare mounting surface
concepts: remove soap dispenser hardware
gasket under the sink for leak prevention
apply plumber's putty in a bead to seal
sections.description: The top soap dispenser is removed to clear space for the filter housing. A gasket is noted, and putty is applied under the sink to ensure a watertight seal during mounting.

sections.title: Secure mounting hardware and assemble compression path
concepts: lock nut under the sink
washers and mounting hardware
compression connection: nut, ferrule, insert
sections.description: Under-sink mounting hardware is installed with a lock nut and washers. The compression connection for the filter’s tubing is assembled with nut, ferrule, and an insert, ensuring a tight, leak-resistant path.

sections.title: Connect cold feed, cut tubing to length, and test
concepts: connect cold-water feed into filter
measure and cut outlet tubing to length
push tubing into connectors
turn on cold valve upstream and test
air/cloudiness on first fill
final leak check
sections.description: The installer completes the remaining connections to the filter: pushing in the cold feed and trimming the outlet tubing to an appropriate length. After re-opening the basement shut-off, the first flow may be cloudy due to air; the setup is tested for leaks and proper operation.
